Socket: A WebSocket client connection, implemented as a duplex stream over a TCP or TLS socket.
Socket.constructor: Open a WebSocket connection to `url`, or wrap an already-connected `opts.socket` when acting as the server side of a handshake.
Socket.ping: Send a WebSocket ping frame with `data` as its payload.
Socket.pong: Send a WebSocket pong frame with `data` as its payload.
Socket.handshake: Perform the client side of the WebSocket opening handshake over `req`, calling `cb` with a `WebSocketError` if the server's response is invalid.
Socket.WebSocketEvents.ping: Emitted when a ping frame is received, with the frame's payload.
Socket.WebSocketEvents.pong: Emitted when a pong frame is received, with the frame's payload.
Socket.WebSocketOptions: `host`/`hostname` (an alias for `host`, for Node.js compatibility), `port`, and `path` address the connection. `secure` uses TLS (`wss:`) for the underlying connection when `true`. `socket` is an already-connected TCP socket to use instead of opening a new connection.
Socket.WebSocketOptions.hostname: Alias for `host`, accepted for Node.js compatibility.
Socket.WebSocketOptions.path: The request path used in the handshake.
Socket.WebSocketOptions.secure: Use TLS (`wss:`) for the underlying connection when `true`.
Socket.WebSocketOptions.socket: An already-connected TCP socket to use instead of opening a new connection.
Server: A WebSocket server that upgrades incoming HTTP or HTTPS connections to WebSocket connections.
Server.constructor: Create a server, optionally backed by `opts.server`, and emit `connection` for each successful WebSocket upgrade.
Server.address: Return the bound address of the underlying TCP server.
Server.close: Stop the server from accepting new connections, calling `cb` once it has closed.
Server.listening: `true` once the underlying server is bound and accepting connections.
Server.ref: Ref the underlying server so it keeps the event loop alive.
Server.handshake: Perform the server side of the WebSocket opening handshake for `req`, writing the `101` upgrade response on `socket` and calling `cb` with a `WebSocketError` on failure.
Server.WebSocketServerEvents.connection: Emitted with the new `WebSocket` and the originating request after a successful handshake.
Server.WebSocketServerEvents.listening: Emitted once the underlying server starts listening.
Server.WebSocketServerOptions: `secure` creates an HTTPS-backed server, accepting `wss:` connections, when `true`.
Server.WebSocketServerOptions.secure: Create an HTTPS-backed server, accepting `wss:` connections, when `true`.
Server.unref: Unref the underlying server so it does not keep the event loop alive on its own.
WebSocketConstructor: The type of the `Socket` class, used to type the global `WebSocket` constructor.
EOL: The line ending (`\r\n`) used when writing the handshake response.
EOF: The blank-line terminator (`\r\n\r\n`) that ends the handshake response headers.
GUID: The WebSocket protocol's fixed GUID, concatenated with the `Sec-WebSocket-Key` to compute the `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` digest.
opcode: The WebSocket frame opcodes (`CONTINUATION`, `TEXT`, `BINARY`, `CLOSE`, `PING`, `PONG`) as defined by RFC 6455.
status: WebSocket close status codes for protocol errors (`PROTOCOL_ERROR`) and oversized messages (`MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE`).
WebSocketError: An error thrown for WebSocket protocol violations, carrying a `code` and a close `status`.
WebSocketError.EXPECTED_CONTINUATION: A fragmented message's next frame was not a continuation frame.
WebSocketError.EXPECTED_MASK: A frame from a client was missing its required mask.
WebSocketError.INCOMPLETE_FRAME: The buffered data does not yet contain a full frame.
WebSocketError.INVALID_ACCEPT_HEADER: The `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` header in the server's handshake response did not match the expected digest.
WebSocketError.INVALID_ENCODING: Data was written with an encoding other than `buffer` or `utf8`.
WebSocketError.INVALID_KEY_HEADER: The `Sec-WebSocket-Key` header was missing or malformed.
WebSocketError.INVALID_OPCODE: A frame was received with an opcode that is not `TEXT` or `BINARY`.
WebSocketError.INVALID_PAYLOAD_LENGTH: A frame's payload length field was invalid.
WebSocketError.INVALID_UPGRADE_HEADER: The `Upgrade` header was missing or not `websocket`.
WebSocketError.NETWORK_ERROR: The underlying HTTP request errored before the handshake completed.
WebSocketError.NOT_CONNECTED: An operation, such as `ping()` or `pong()`, was attempted before the socket finished connecting.
WebSocketError.UNEXPECTED_CONTINUATION: A continuation frame was received without a preceding fragmented frame.
WebSocketError.UNEXPECTED_CONTROL: A control frame was received while a fragmented message was in progress.
WebSocketError.UNEXPECTED_RSV1: A frame was received with the reserved RSV1 bit set.
WebSocketError.UNEXPECTED_RSV2: A frame was received with the reserved RSV2 bit set.
WebSocketError.UNEXPECTED_RSV3: A frame was received with the reserved RSV3 bit set.
